assign.brief: Owner (via vscode-mastermind): close the drawer after ?drawer=ai or a resize and the page keeps its squeezed width, the ☰ stays displaced. Close must clear every size it set, whatever opened it; one function owns the state; headless regression test.

log.msg: reproduced headless at 1920: a reload with the drawer open (or ?drawer=ai) writes --drawer on <body> because build() ran before .app existed; close() cleared only .app, so .app inherited 304px of padding and the ☰ stayed at x=1608. Escape does not close the drawer at all (not asked; noted).

fix 41518975 in worktree drawer-close: token() is the one writer of --drawer/--drawer-w, always on the current .app, clearing any copy on <body>. regression.mjs: live 4/8 fail, fix 8/8 pass. Shots: shots/after-close-1920.png, shots/drawer-open-400.png

findings.text: There is no requirements.md in this task folder, so I checked the work against the owner's ask (asks.jsonl line 163, "closing it sometimes doesn't give the page its space back") and the brief in task.jsonl line 1. The fix answers both: one function writes the two size tokens, and closing clears them wherever they were written.

The root cause is right and the fix sits where it belongs. When the page reloads with the drawer open, `build()` runs before `.app` exists and wrote `--drawer` on `<body>`; `close()` then cleared only `.app`. Now `token()` (ext/drawer/drawer.js:35) always clears `<body>` and writes on the current `.app`, and the move into `.app` (drawer.js:113-119) carries over the width and the open state. I found no other file that writes `--drawer` or `--drawer-w`, so "one writer" holds.

A smaller patch would have worked: copy the two tokens from `<body>` to `.app` in the move block, and leave the other writers alone. `token()` costs about the same and also covers a resize that happens before `.app` exists, so I would keep it.

The screenshot shots/after-close-1920.png shows the closed page at full width with ☰ back in the top-right corner. task.jsonl records that regression.mjs failed 4 of 8 cases before the fix and passed 8 of 8 after it.

regression.mjs:6 imports Playwright from a hard-coded path under one user's AppData, so the test runs only on this machine. That is acceptable for a test kept in the task folder, but the readme now links to it as "the regression test", so a reader may expect it to run anywhere.

In regression.mjs:26-33, three cases are `null`, and what they do is worked out from words in their names ("drag", "☰ close"). Giving each case its own small function, like the other four, would be easier to follow.
The task log says Escape does not close the drawer. That was not part of the ask and has been logged; it is worth a separate small task.
